summary: Long-tail hangs and spike in median latency traced to aggressive client retries after soft quota signals (missing Retry-After)
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple Lumena Health services reported long-tail request hangs and elevated token latency beginning 2026-03-11 08:30 UTC. Customers observed requests that previously completed in <200ms now intermittently hang for 5-15s before eventual failure or 429. The symptom profile looked indistinguishable from an inference runtime slowdown at first glance.

Impact:
- A set of API routes used by Lumena Health (real-time summarization) saw a 10-25% increase in end-to-end p95/p99 latency windows during their peak.
- UI load spikes and some user-facing timeouts triggered customer-side retries, amplifying traffic.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east), routes: /v1/generate, /v1/streaming-chat
- Customer using Redwood SDK v0.9.2 pinned to model redwood/gptx-3b on our Dedicated pool

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Under normal peak traffic, service returns intermittent 429 responses tied to quota enforcement window (soft quota enforcement).
2) 429 responses were missing or had inconsistent Retry-After headers for a small fraction of responses due to a gateway edge-case for pooled connections.
3) Customer SDK (v0.9.2) did not honor Retry-After when absent and immediately retried with high concurrency, creating a retry surge.
4) Retry surge caused request queueing at the serving-runtime and larger tails on latency distributions, which in turn led more requests to hit quota gates -> feedback loop.

Observed logs / signals:
- api-gateway logs (2026-03-11 08:28-09:00 UTC): elevated 429 rate for Lumena routes, ~0.8% -> 3.6%
- serving-runtime traces: request_queue_time p99 rose from 20ms -> 8.2s in affected window
- metric: throttle_signal_no_retry_header increased for some edge ELB connections (internal metric)
- customer-side logs show immediate retry attempts within 50-100ms of original request failure

Investigation notes / hypothesis:
- Primary hypothesis: missing or inconsistent Retry-After header combined with SDK behavior resulted in retry amplification; this created a feedback loop that looked like a runtime latency regression.
- Secondary contributing factor: Dedicated pool had a short burst-window enforcement that emits a soft throttle signal without strong client-visible signals in some connection paths.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- API gateway rule patched at 2026-03-11 10:15 UTC to ensure Retry-After header is returned for all soft-quota 429s (edge fix rolled to us-east).
- Support provided Lumena with a recommended SDK configuration to enable exponential backoff and jitter; Lumena applied a temporary client-side rate limiter within their service while we rolled the gateway fix.

Permanent remediation / engineering actions:
- Engineering created PR platform/pull/4123 to harden gateway behavior and add a test that validates Retry-After propagation for pooled connection scenarios. PR merged and rolled to prod on 2026-03-12 04:20 UTC.
- SDK team published patch v0.9.3 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/589) to respect Retry-After when present and to implement conservative default backoff when Retry-After missing.
- Added a dashboard tile and alert for throttle_signal_no_retry_header to catch regressions early.

Customer communication and status:
- 2026-03-11 11:00 UTC: initial triage call with Lumena support/engineering; shared mitigation steps and accepted temporary limiter.
- 2026-03-12 12:00 UTC: verified customer reports latency returned to baseline after gateway fix + SDK bump.

Next steps / follow-ups (action items):
- [ENG] Add integration test for Retry-After propagation across edge pools (owner: Ethan Brooks, ETA: 2026-03-20).
- [SDK] Backport conservative retry defaults to older SDK minor release used by some customers (owner: Claire Zhang, ETA: 2026-03-18).
- [SUPPORT] Reach out to other mid-tier dedicated customers with SDK <0.9.3 to recommend upgrade (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-03-16).

Resolution summary:
- Root cause: client retry amplification caused by missing Retry-After header in a subset of soft-quota 429 responses + SDK aggressive retry defaults.
- Fixes: gateway propagation fix + SDK patch + added monitoring/alerts. Customer latency impact mitigated and verified.
